concerns.quote: The discharge planning in relation to Mr Slater was overshadowed by the impasse in clinical opinion and the length of time it took to resolve this. No doubt because of the difficulties to resolve Gareth's situation there was a failure to actually carry out the important task of discharge planning. No care plan was in place for Gareth, merely a recognition of the conditions of his Community Treatment Order.
There was no Section 17 discharge planning meeting.
concerns.hazard: absence of Section 17 discharge planning meeting

concerns.quote: There was no further assessment since 2011 of Gareth's ability to live independently (as opposed to in supported accommodation which had failed).
concerns.hazard: lack of further assessment of independent living ability

concerns.quote: There was no attempt to involve Gareth's family in the discharge of Gareth.
concerns.hazard: lack of family involvement in discharge

concerns.quote: There was no use of extended periods of leave for Gareth to assess his ability to manage his tenancy.
concerns.hazard: lack of extended leave to assess tenancy management

concerns.quote: Onhis discharge the flat was unfurnished, without carpets and he was not able to reside there. The condition of the flat at the time of Gareth's death remained sparsely furnished with a large water leak in the kitchen.

concerns.quote: The inquest heard evidence that the Mental Health Trust had not introduced one IT system across the Trust, which impacted on information sharing between professionals involved in his care

there was no clear system for the primary and secondary mental health services of the mental health trust ,Pennine Care, to develop a joined up discharge plan following a stay on the mental health ward
concerns.hazard: absence of clear discharge planning system

concerns.quote: a need for a type of mental health support service had been identified by the mental health trust Pennine Care but it could not be delivered because the Trust had not been commissioned to deliver the service
concerns.hazard: lack of commissioned mental health support service

concerns.quote: Tameside Hospital cannot change their electronic booking in/triage system to allow them to include drop down boxes for key information such as the fact that Police Officers have brought an individual to the Hospital because it is a national IT system
concerns.hazard: inability to capture police officer information in booking system

links.explanation: Both reports highlight problems with discharge planning for mental health patients within Pennine Care NHS Trust. The earlier report cites specific failures in carrying out discharge planning due to clinical disagreement, while the later report points to the absence of a coordinated system for primary and secondary services to create a joined‑up discharge plan.
